# #205 — append_session_event stores created_by=rico for Nagatha namespace writes

## Problem
After rtech-hermes PR #213, Nagatha writes Open Brain session events with the correct namespace and source, but Open Brain still stores created_by=rico.

## Evidence
Post-deploy Nagatha canary after rtech-hermes main 1b85982 and rollout /mnt/collab/agent-backups/agents/nagatha/logs/rollouts/20260626T020928Z:

Command:
`mcp2cli open-brain session_context --params '{"namespace":"nagatha","channel_id":"1511959782943363123","include_events":true,"event_limit":5}'`

Latest lane/event excerpt:
- lane.namespace: nagatha
- lane.agent: nagatha
- lane.current_context_md begins: Agent: nagatha / Platform: discord / Project: hermes
- latest event id: 4777184d-c1a0-46e8-93b9-c77915c1a73d
- latest event source: nagatha
- latest event created_by: rico
- trace id: NAGATHA_INBOX_OK_0608C9FA

Nagatha-local service check reports:
`mcp2cli services` -> open-brain description: "Open Brain MCP via Nagatha token".

## Expected
For a write scoped to namespace=nagatha and sent by Nagatha's configured mcp2cli/OpenBrain credential, created_by should be nagatha, or Open Brain should expose a separate actor/client field that makes why created_by=rico explicit.

## Why it matters
The agent memory setup relies on namespace/source/actor attribution to audit which agent wrote facts. rtech-hermes can now control source=nagatha, but created_by still makes the durable row look Rico-authored.

## Not fixed by rtech-hermes #213
rtech-hermes #213 changed provider fallback so generic gateway identity no longer sends source=default. It does not control server-side created_by attribution.
